task.description: Fix the sole blocking finding from RELEASE-VALIDATOR's Step 5 FAIL (commit 06fb22e): AC5 ('exactly an explicit allowlist of fields, demonstrated by a test asserting the full key set of the response body') was only satisfied by presence + named-exclusion checks, not a full key-set assertion. Add the missing assertion; no other AC was in question (all other 5 confirmed MET independently, including two separate AC2 mutation probes).
acceptance_criteria: AC5: response allowlist -- exactly 8 keys, full key-set assertion in the test, not just presence checks (INV-2)

result.summary: Added a full key-set equality assertion (`Map.keys(body) |> Enum.sort() == ["auth_source", "display_name", "email", "id", "inserted_at", "status", "updated_at", "username"]`) to every AC1 end-to-end test in test/letflow/routers/identity_test.exs whose response body goes through user_map/1 -- create (line ~79), list (asserted per-item over body["items"]), get, patch, and status-update. Followed this codebase's existing full-key-set-assertion convention from test/letflow/api/error_test.exs:153-157 (`Error.conflict("x") |> decode() |> Map.keys() |> Enum.sort()`). Confirmed the expected 8-key set directly against lib/letflow/routers/identity.ex's user_map/1 (lines 322-333) before writing the assertions, rather than trusting the handoff's suggested list. No other test, no application code, no design doc touched -- git diff confined to this one file. Ran `mix test test/letflow/routers/identity_test.exs` myself: 23 tests, 0 failures (matches the pre-rework count; no new tests added, existing ones strengthened).
result.next_action: Route to TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (Step 3b re-review) to confirm the strengthened assertions satisfy AC5, then TEST-RUNNER (Step 4) and RELEASE-VALIDATOR (Step 5) again before DOC-UPDATER.
